message.content:
**Weekly Nutrient Guidance for a Small Outdoor Cactus in Arizona During Summer** | Item | Typical Recommendation | |------|------------------------| | **Fertilizer Type** | Balanced NPK (10‑20‑10) “slow‑release” granules or liquid micro‑fertilizer formulated for succulents. | | **Application Frequency** | Once every 4–6 weeks (i.e., roughly once a month), not truly *weekly*—succulents don’t need frequent feeding because their root systems are shallow and they store moisture efficiently. | | **Amount Per Pot Size** | • < 5 L pot: ~¼ tsp of granular fertilizer.
• 5–15 L pot: ~½ tsp.
• > 15 L pot: ¾–1 tsp.
(If you’re using a liquid feed, dilute one full dose in 8 L of water.) | | **Seasonal Adjustment** | In hot Arizona summers, reduce fertilization slightly compared to late spring. Over‑feeding can cause salt buildup and damage roots. | | **Signs of Adequate Nutrition** | Healthy greenish stems, steady growth, absence of brown tips or stunted development. | ### Why Not Weekly? Cacti absorb most of their needed minerals from the soil over longer periods. Frequent application leads to excess salts accumulating around the roots, which can burn them especially under intense sun. A monthly schedule balances nutrition while protecting against salt stress. --- #### Quick Reference Cheat Sheet ``` Pot Size Fertilizer Dose Dilution Ratio (Liquid) ----------------------------------------------- ≤5 L 0.25 tsp 1:32 (one dose in 8 L water) 5–15 L 0.50 tsp 1:16 ≥15 L 0.75–1 tsp 1:8 ``` Feel free to let me know your exact pot volume or whether this cactus is indoors vs outdoors so I can fine‑tune the dosage!
